EU/EEA.basis: Directive 2006/116/EC, Article 1(1), (2), (8): life plus 70 years, term calculated from 1 January following the relevant event. Lermontov died in 1841; the ordinary term ended 31 December 1911 and the poems entered the public domain on 1 January 1912.
EU/EEA.posthumous_publication: «Утёс» and «Выхожу один я на дорогу» were first published in 1843, only two years after the author's death, during the ordinary copyright term; the 25-year right for first publication of previously unpublished works after copyright expiry (Article 4) does not apply.
EU/EEA.transition: Article 10(2) applies the Directive's terms to works protected in at least one Member State on 1 July 1995; these works were already out of copyright long before that date.

Germany.basis: UrhG Section 64: 70 years after author's death. Section 70: any qualifying scientific edition has a 25-year related-right term. The 1901 editions are long outside that term; even if the 1989 source edition for «Утёс» qualifies, its Section 70 term expired by the end of 2014. No editorial apparatus is reproduced.

Netherlands.basis: Official Business.gov.nl guidance: copyright lasts 70 years after the creator's death, counted from 1 January of the following year. The author's term ended 31 December 1911. The poems were lawfully published during the term; no previously-unpublished posthumous first-publication right is relied upon.

Russia.basis: Civil Code Article 1281 sets life plus 70 years. Federal Law No. 231-FZ Article 6 applies the new 70-year terms only when the prior 50-year term had not expired by 1 January 1993. For an author who died in 1841, the earlier 50-year term had expired in 1891, so the transition does not revive protection.

United States.basis: 17 U.S.C. §104A requires a restored foreign work not to be in the public domain in its source country through expiration of term. The source country is the Russian Empire / successor Russian jurisdiction and the author's term had expired there long before 1996; however, the historical source-country/succession analysis has not been independently certified by U.S. counsel.
